title: Primary Operations Progression: China, England and US Common Core Baseline
purpose: Provide a comparison spine for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and formal written methods without forcing false grade equivalence.

CN.placement: Grade 1 upper confirmed for early number/addition/subtraction units; later exact grade sequence pending current-volume verification.

UK.placement: Year 1 begins within 20; Year 2 consolidates facts and two-digit calculation with concrete, pictorial and mental methods.

US.placement: Grade 1 develops strategy-based addition/subtraction within 20 and selected calculation within 100; Grade 2 extends to 1000 through place-value-based strategies.

CN.verified_signal: Current PEP redesign integrates previously separate within-10,000 addition/subtraction units.
CN.publication_constraint: Do not publish an exact current grade for formal algorithm introduction until the current 12th-series volume and teacher guide are verified.

progression: Year 2: column recording prepares for formal methods
Year 3: formal columnar addition/subtraction up to 3 digits
Year 4: formal columnar methods up to 4 digits
Year 5–6: fluent application with increasingly large numbers and multi-step problems
Grade 1–2: strategies, models, place-value reasoning and written-method connections
Grade 3: fluency within 1000 using strategies and algorithms; no single standard algorithm mandated
Grade 4: standard algorithm required for multi-digit whole-number addition/subtraction
Grade 5: decimals continue through models, reasoning and written-method connections

strands.comparison_insight: England makes formal columnar addition/subtraction explicit earlier than Common Core's mandatory standard-algorithm endpoint, while Common Core intentionally preserves multiple strategies for longer. Exact current PEP timing is not yet safe to claim.

signature: exploration through operations, experiment and reasoning
CN.note: Current PEP exact grade-by-grade placement requires volume-level verification.

progression: Year 1: grouping, sharing, doubling and arrays with teacher support
Year 2: 2, 5 and 10 tables plus arrays, repeated addition and inverse relations
Year 3: 3, 4 and 8 tables; two-digit by one-digit calculation begins moving toward written methods
Grade 2: equal groups and rectangular arrays as foundations
Grade 3: formal meaning of products and quotients, equal groups, arrays, sharing/grouping, fact fluency within 100

strands.comparison_insight: Both England and Common Core explicitly establish multiplication/division through grouping, sharing and arrays before multi-digit algorithms. The current PEP series also describes a stronger connected-content and exploratory design, so MathBridge should avoid the stereotype that Chinese mathematics is algorithm-first by definition.

CN.verified_signal: PEP reports integration of the former two-digit × two-digit and three-digit × two-digit units in the new series.
CN.interpretation: The redesign is explicitly intended to support logical connection, analogy and transfer across related content.

progression: Year 3: movement from mental calculation toward written two-digit × one-digit methods
Year 4: formal layout for two-/three-digit × one-digit; short multiplication
Year 5: formal multiplication up to four-digit × one-/two-digit, including long multiplication
Year 6: long multiplication maintained as a fluent four-operation method
Grade 3: facts/properties and one-digit × multiples of 10
Grade 4: multi-digit multiplication through place value, properties, equations, arrays and area models; standard algorithm not yet required
Grade 5: fluent multi-digit multiplication using the standard algorithm

strands.comparison_insight: A key England/US distinction is algorithm timing: England explicitly develops formal written multiplication during Years 3–5, while Common Core preserves model/property-based multi-digit strategies through Grade 4 before requiring the standard algorithm in Grade 5.

CN.publication_constraint: Current PEP volume/teacher-guide evidence is required before claiming the precise introduction point for formal written division or long division.

progression: Year 3: reliable written division begins from two-digit ÷ one-digit contexts
Year 4: short division with exact answers
Year 5: short division up to four-digit dividends by one digit with contextual remainder interpretation
Year 6: long division and short division with two-digit divisors, interpreting remainders appropriately
Grade 3: division meaning/facts within 100
Grade 4: quotients/remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors using place-value/property strategies plus arrays/area models
Grade 5: up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors through place-value/property strategies; standard algorithm not yet the Grade 5 requirement
Grade 6: standard-algorithm fluency endpoint for multi-digit division in the Common Core progression

strands.comparison_insight: England names formal short and long division methods explicitly in primary statutory guidance; Common Core delays the standard-algorithm endpoint and requires explanation through place value, properties and representations during earlier multi-digit division.
